elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 13.6.1 is left unchanged and provides that the Agreement "shall be interpreted, governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, United States"; no New York choice of law is introduced.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: The inserted forum in 13.7.1 is "the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware", not New York County.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.6.1: "governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, United States", with conflicts rules excluded; deterministic check "governing law within the accepted set" passes. Patent-inventorship/construction provisos are customary IP carve-outs and do not displace Delaware law for the Agreement.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Amended 13.7.1 now allows either Party to "elect to submit the Dispute to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware", and amended 13.7.3 states "No Dispute shall be submitted to arbitration, and Schedule 13.7.3 shall not apply.", removing the redacted-seat arbitration path so the Delaware court forum is the operative and exclusive merits forum, matching Delaware governing law.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: Delaware law was already in the accepted set and is untouched, and the redline supplies the missing accepted court forum by making unresolved Disputes subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts.
Preferred is not met and was not targeted: neither New York law nor New York County exclusive jurisdiction appears anywhere in the rendered language.

Switching off arbitration in 13.7.3 is necessary, not extra: leaving the arbitration mechanic and Schedule 13.7.3 in force would create a retained sentence contradicting the new exclusive court forum, and the schedule's seat is redacted so it could not be confirmed as an accepted venue.

Minimality holds: only the forum words in 13.7.1 and the conflicting arbitration sentence in 13.7.3 changed. The Senior Officer escalation mechanic, the [***] period, the Section 13.7.2 patent carve-out, the 13.6.1 governing-law sentence with its IP provisos and CISG exclusion, and the Section 13.11 equitable-relief carve-out are all retained; no survival tails, cost-shifting, procedures or other boilerplate were added.

Intent is preserved: the 13.6.2 service-of-process reference to "any such court" now has a proper antecedent jurisdiction clause, the retained "which shall fully and finally settle the Dispute" reads coherently against a court election, and the residual heading "Arbitration" in 13.7.3 is cosmetic only. Drafter should still spot-check for any other cross-references to Schedule 13.7.3 or to an "arbitrator" elsewhere in the document (e.g., in payment-dispute or audit provisions) and conform them, since those paragraphs were not supplied here.
